articles.title: Mother sought advice from Alan Jones after broadcaster’s alleged indecent assault of her son, court hears
articles.summary:
Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching

The mother of the youngest alleged victim of Alan Jones continued to seek advice from the broadcaster…

blocks.text: The mother of the youngest alleged victim of Alan Jones continued to seek advice from the broadcaster after the teenager was allegedly indecently assaulted at Jones’s Fitzroy Falls farm, a Sydney court has heard.

The divorced mother told the Downing Centre court she had developed a pattern of not trusting herself and she continued her correspondence with Jones because: “I knew he knew about everything; he had an opinion about everything.
“I was in a web of dependency with Mr Jones,” the witness said on her last day in the witness box on Friday.
She previously said she corresponded with Jones after he allegedly kissed the 17-year-old and put his tongue inside his mouth out of fear Jones would withdraw his financial support.
During cross examination, defence barrister Claire O’Neill suggested the mother continued to correspond with Jones not because she was scared but because she wanted more money out of him.
O’Neill asked: “You did not continue to communicate with Mr Jones because you were scared of his influence over your finances, did you?”
The witness replied: “I absolutely was.”
Her son, complainant A, is one of five men who allege Jones, 85, sexually touched or indecently assaulted them between 2003 and 2020. All five have now completed their evidence.
Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching.

Under cross-examination by the defence, the witness agreed she wrote to Jones about her son’s late university application, a superannuation payment, outstanding legal fees and attaining a Sydney Cricket Ground membership for her son.
She was shown an email in which she provided Jones with an update on her son’s university application. The defence asked: “You wanted to lay the groundwork for having Mr Jones pay the [legal] bill?
The mother said the suggestion was “absolute rubbish” and she was “proud of him” for finishing year 12 under difficult circumstances and wanted to convey that in the email.
She agreed she sent Jones information about the cost of repairs to her Land Rover but denied she was asking him to pay the bill.
“You have told lies in this court about why you continued to have contact with Jones?” O’Neill asked.
The witness replied: “Absolutely disagree, that’s rubbish.”
O’Neill: “You were taking advantage of Mr Jones’s generosity for as long as you could?”
Witness: “Absolute rubbish.”
When she was asked why she shared personal information with Jones about the deterioration of her relationship with her son she became emotional.
“My son, who was a child, suffered trauma and didn’t share it with anyone and it had an effect on his relationship with me and a lot of other people.”
Asked by prosecutor Georgina Wright what that trauma was, she replied: “I was referring to what happened to him at Fitzroy Falls”.
The trial continues.
Listen to the podcast Alan Jones on Trial.

articles.title: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
articles.summary: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.

image.caption: The crowds at the rally were optimistic that they would be free of populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in a matter of daysImage: Uros Arsic/REUTERS

blocks.text: Over a hundred thousand of Serbians took to the streets in support of Serbia's protesting youth movement on Thursday, in what was the final campaign rally ahead of a pivotal election challenge to the Balkan nation's populist strongman, Aleksandar Vucic.

Crowds poured into Belgrade's central square from all directions and filled up several blocks around the area. Independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings estimated about 150,000 people were at the rally.

blocks.caption: Protesters filled Belgrade's Slavija square and its surrounding streetsImage: Marko Djurica/REUTERS

blocks.text: The optimistic crowds chanted "victory" ahead of Sunday's crunch vote which comes after two years of student-led protests against Vucic. It was triggered by a 2024 collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated Novi Sad railway station which killed 16 people.
The anti-corruption movement, led by university students, has since snowballed from demands for an independent investigation into the incident, into calls for early elections.
The scandals that rocked Serbia and are shaping the election
What happened at the protest?
The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, is the veteran leader's biggest threat.
Thousands supporting it flocked to Belgrade's streets on Thursday.

"I came to support the Student List because young people finally gave me hope that it is possible to live in a normal country," 47-year-old Marija Nedeljkovic Radic told the French AFP news agency as she arrived for the students' rally.
"Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible," she said.

blocks.caption: The Students List's election ticket is polling neck and neck with Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive PartyImage: DW

blocks.text: "We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours," university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of 250 candidates on the Student List, told the crowd who chanted "Victory, victory!"
"You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!"
How has Vucic responded?
Vucic has dominated Serbian politics for over a decade now, either as prime minister or president of the Balkan country.
As pressure from the protests mounted, he announced a snap election last month. He has resigned as president, but many argue it is a tactical move so that he could run for prime minister.
This is now the biggest electoral challenge his party, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), has faced since it was elected into power in 2012.
The leader, meanwhile, has regularly accused the students movement of being a foreign-funded coup.

"Let us never forget how they tried to bring down our state. Let us always protect and defend it," Vucic said to a sports hall full of supporters on Thursday. "Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!"
Serbia's student revolt: Will it bring about change?
Worries of post-result unrest
Days before the vote, Serbian civil societies warned that conditions for "free and fair election" were lacking.

"This assessment is not based on isolated incidents, opposition claims or political disagreement with the government," a joint statement by 24 organisations said, arguing it was supported by documented findings.

Analysts warn that a close election result could lead to post-election instability, if both sides declare victory. Vucic, who controls the Serbian police, has said he would quash any unrest after the vote.

While several minor parties are also in the race for premiership, observers say that there is a referendum-like atmosphere between Vucic and the students' movement which could sideline other parties in the 250-member parliament.

articles.title: Duterte ICC trial: Prosecutors seek to admit three witness accounts
articles.summary: One witness discusses 13 killings charged under Count 3, including a death during a police “One Time Big Time” operation.

blocks.text: October 23, 2026 | 10:35am
ICC proceedings tied to former president Rodrigo Duterte's so-called drug war scrutinize command responsibility, police operations and the families' long-running calls for justice.
Philstar.com illustration

MANILA, Philippines — International Criminal Court prosecutors have asked judges to admit the recorded statements of three witnesses who they say can describe the policy to "neutralize" alleged drug suspects under former president Rodrigo Duterte.

One witness speaks about 13 of the killings charged against Duterte, including one during a police "One Time Big Time" operation, according to the redacted version of the court filing dated October 21 and signed by Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.
The three witnesses, all women, were already on the prosecution's witness list. The defense has known since August 31 that prosecutors planned to present them under this procedure.

Prosecutors are asking the court to allow transcripts of their earlier interviews with investigators to be admitted as evidence in place of most of their direct examination, saying this would save court time.

Under Rule 68(3) of the court's rules, each witness must still appear in court, confirm her statement is accurate and consent to its use. Duterte's lawyers can cross-examine them, and the judges and lawyers for victims can still question them.
All three accounts relate to Count 3, which covers killings in barangay "clearance" operations against alleged small-time drug users and pushers from about July 2016 to September 2018.

When the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I confirmed the charges against Duterte on April 23, Count 3 covered 45 victims, 43 of whom were killed. Count 1 covers 19 killings in Davao City from 2013 to 2016, when Duterte was mayor, and Count 2 covers 14 killings of alleged "high-value targets" in 2016 and 2017.
Pattern of killings
The identities of the three witnesses were withheld in the public document.
The statement of one witness, who is labelled in the filing as "P-0008," comes from two interviews with prosecution investigators.
In several of the 13 killings she discusses, she allegedly described events before the victims died. Names, dates and places are redacted in the public filing.

The filing does not say where or when the "One Time Big Time" operation took place. Police in the Philippines are known to have used the term for simultaneous, large-scale anti-drug sweeps, where deadly shootouts also occur.
Prosecutors said P-0008's evidence shows the "modus operandi and pattern of violence" police used against alleged criminals.
Another witness, labelled "P-1164," spoke about three charged killings by police.
Meanwhile, "P-1303" gives evidence about an individual who was shot dead by police, but her relationship to him is redacted in the filing. Prosecutors said her account relates to one charged killing.
Prosecutors said the three accounts are internally consistent and match evidence expected from other witnesses, including "P-0003," who is due to testify in person.
They said the evidence also helps prove that the killings were part of a widespread or systematic attack on civilians, a requirement for crimes against humanity.
The prosecutors said the three witnesses will show there was a policy to "neutralise" alleged criminals through violence, including murder.
All three women were told their interviews were voluntary and were informed of their rights, and each confirmed she answered of her own free will, the filing said.

articles.summary: The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan

blocks.text: THREAT. Typhoon Champi swirls over the Philippine Sea, as seen from space on October 22, 2026 in this screengrab taken from a handout GIF image.
via REUTERS
The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan

items: Taiwan shut down on October 23 ahead of Typhoon Champi, which, despite weakening, is expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain, particularly to northeastern areas.
The storm, previously a super typhoon, is forecast to pass off the northeastern coast of Taiwan and move towards southern Japan, with significant impacts expected over the next two days.
One fatality and numerous injuries have been reported, prompting evacuations and emergency preparations, including the cancellation of flights and the closure of financial markets.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

YILAN, Taiwan – Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday, October 23, ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph near its center, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).

The storm was about 320 km east of Taiwan’s southern tip, the CWA said. The storm’s forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.

blocks.caption: Typhoon Rosal still bringing moderate to heavy rain to Batanes

blocks.text: One person was killed and 94 were injured in Taiwan, where the government said almost 1,300 people had been evacuated from mountainous areas.

Coastal towns received mobile phone alerts warning of gusts exceeding 150 kph and urging residents to seek immediate shelter, while nearly 3 feet of rain was forecast for northern mountain areas, including around Taipei.

In the northeastern county of Yilan, where strong winds and heavy showers were intensifying and the typhoon was forecast to pass close by later on Friday, authorities distributed sandbags and put amphibious vehicles and inflatable rescue boats on standby.

“When necessary, the military will come in to help people, including using amphibious vehicles for evacuations or disaster relief,” said Lee Ming-chen, head of the port town of Suao, which was badly flooded in previous typhoons.
Taiwan forecasters said the storm’s radius was around 320 km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.
Taiwan’s financial markets also closed on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal.
The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were canceled for Friday, along with 669 international ones. The north-south high-speed rail service was operating as usual.
In the capital Taipei there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was working, albeit with reduced service.
Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.
The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan’s westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Airbnb scraps guest checkout chores such as cleaning
articles.summary: Under new rules, guests will no longer have to do tasks that cleaners would normally handle. Hosts can now only make "reasonable" requests, such as leaving dirty dishes in the sink and sorting trash…

image.caption: Asking guests to do cleaning tasks can negatively impact their stay, Airbnb warns hostsImage: Jonas Been Henriksen/NTB/picture alliance

blocks.text: Chores such as washing dishes, stripping beds and taking out the trash at the end of your Airbnb stay will soon be a thing of the past.
Under new rules unveiled this week, the short-term rental platform says hosts should only make "reasonable" requests of guests.

Airbnb said hosts are generally not allowed to "ask guests to complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner, including stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes."

blocks.caption: 'Unreasonable' demands like changing the sheets are being scrappedImage: Sviatlana Barysenka/Zoonar/picture alliance

blocks.text: Why did Airbnb introduce the new rules?
Checkout chores have been a contentious issue for guests, especially in cases where they are also charged cleaning fees.
Airbnb has previously admitted that such fees can create confusion between guests and hosts.
"Guests expect checkout to be relatively simple, and most want to avoid unexpected chores," Airbnb said in a message to hosts on the platform.
"Asking them to do things a cleaner should handle can negatively affect their stay and your reviews."

blocks.caption: Guests will still be expected to leave dirty dishes in the sink or dishwasherImage: Thomas Trutschel/photothek/picture alliance

blocks.text: The new rules come amid growing protests against housing shortages in many European cities, with protesters arguing that short-term rentals such as Airbnb have pushed them out of their own cities.
In September, the European Commission proposed more restrictions on Airbnb and other short-term rental companies in tourist hubs.
What else do the new Airbnb rules for hosts say?
Guests can still be asked to leave dirty dishes in the sink, to gather used towels and separate trash and recyclables, for example.
Hosts can also require guests to put trash in animal-proof containers areas where bears are active or ask them to "limit shower time due to local drought-related water restrictions."
But hosts will no longer be allowed to ban guests from using amenities listed in the property description, such as air conditioners, nor will they be allowed to fine guests.
Instead, hosts must seek compensation for any damage from insurance that the platform provides.
The new policy applies to bookings starting on November 20.

“Definitely not. That’s why I got her in the first place,” he said.
“No. Not gentler,” Santiago said.
If there is one thing I remember about Leah from when I met her 29 years ago, it is that she was anything but fragile or dainty.

blocks.caption: PMA’s first female summa cum laude takes command of cadets

blocks.text: She was small and thin at the time, but you could tell she was tough. Her female mistahs were sporting the Demi Moore haircut then, but not her. The hairstyle she had during her installation as the first female commandant of cadets at the PMA was the same one she had when she graduated third in the PMA Kalasag-Lahi Class of 1997.

Right after graduation, she was sent to the battlefield in Mindanao. I remember that she belonged to a team that infiltrated the Abu Sayyaf. For a woman doing that at the time, spying on the group was a life-and-death undertaking. Her exploits caught the attention of the Army chief then, retired general Roy Cimatu, who included her among his aides when he became chief of staff.
Now Santiago is on the path to follow suit. Only the signature of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is needed to make her the first female PMA graduate to become a general.
The announcement of her appointment as commandant of cadets was made on September 26, giving Santiago time to prepare.
One thoughtful gesture was her invitation to all her female classmates.

There were 17 of them when they entered Fort del Pilar in April 1993. They were called the Rasul Ladies, after the late senator Santanina Rasul and Republic Act 7192, or the Women in Development and Nation Building Act of 1992.

The PMA built separate barracks for women and added female tactical officers, but these measures were not enough to keep all of them. Some were wooed by their upperclassmen and eventually decided to leave the academy.
Over the next four years, only seven remained.
I can’t recall who first called them the “Magnificent 7,” but the name stuck.
Last Saturday, October 17, two of them joined Santiago at Yap Hall.

blocks.caption: MEMORY LANE. The ‘Magnificent 7,’ which includes Colonel Leah Lorenzo-Santiago. courtesy of Andy Zapata

blocks.text: Maria Victoria Blancaflor-Agoncillo remained in the Philippine Army and became a tank commander. In 2000, she took part in an operation that overran the Moro Islamic Liberation Front‘s Camp Rajamuda, earning the Gold Cross Medal.
She later rose to lead the National Capital Region’s Regional Community Defense Group. Vicky is also an aspiring writer. Last month, she even made time to fangirl over Jessica Zafra.

Marissa Arlene Andres-Martinez remained in the Philippine Navy. By 2022, she was serving as assistant chief of fleet staff for plans (F-5) of the Philippine Fleet. She also serves as a Navy spokesperson.
Santiago also invited about 100 female military officers to the photo opportunity. There are now about 800 female military officers considered part of the Rasul Ladies.
Santiago said she plans to bring together all the “Magnificent 7.”
The other members have taken different paths since their days at the academy.

Ma. Consuelo “Bon” Nunag-Castillo remained in the Philippine Air Force and became the first female pilot of the 205th Tactical Helicopter Wing. She later flew with the Presidential Airlift Wing and held senior positions in the defense establishment and the Air Force.
Aireen Somera became a PAF pilot but resigned because of health issues. She married a pilot classmate who also left the military for commercial aviation.
Sheryl Jane Uy-Cabasang suffered serious injuries in a vehicular accident shortly after graduation and was placed on complete disability discharge.
Santiago said Jane was paralyzed from the neck down and is still undergoing rehabilitation. Somera developed arthritis, which forced her to give up flying.
Arlene Orejana-Trillanes resigned from the service and later became dean of a computer college at the National University. She is married to former senator Antonio Trillanes IV.
It would be nice if their reunion happened at the PMA, where their roller-coaster journey began. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Brazil’s election and the battle for the Amazon – podcast
articles.summary: Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips, heads to Roraima to hear what’s at stake for the rainforest and the communities that live there in the Brazilian presidential runoff…
articles.byline: Presented by Helen Pidd with Tom Phillips; produced by Ivor Manley, Eli Block and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent

blocks.text: For the Amazon and the communities who live there, the stakes in Sunday’s Brazilian presidential election runoff could scarcely be higher.

Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips heads to Roraima, the country’s most northern state, to hear from voters, preachers and politicians in a region that heavily backed Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

He finds them all hopeful that the far-right candidate will bring back the mining that his father Jair so heartily encouraged when in power in an administration that oversaw the felling of 11m acres (4.5m hectares) of rainforest.
Tom also meets Indigenous activists determined to fight back even if the Bolsonaros take power again.
Helen Pidd asks what it will all mean, not only for Brazil but also for the climate crisis more broadly.

blocks.text: Published October 23, 2026 9:55am
Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang on Friday denied involvement in the attempted smuggling of P3.5 billion worth of illegal drugs from Laos to the Philippines.
“Wala po itong katotohanan (there is no truth to this),” Rimbang said in a video posted on his social media page.

“‘Yung sinasabi po nila na [nag] import po tayo nung sa Laos, hindi po totoo ‘yun. Wala po akong nakausap na any government dito sa Pilipinas o mga tao dito sa Pilipinas para magpunta sa Laos o magdala dito ng kahit anong bagay na makakasira sa ating bansa,” he added.

(What they are saying about us importing that from Laos is not true. I have not spoken to any government or any people here in the Philippines about going to Laos or bringing anything here that could harm our country.)
Last week, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla tagged Rimbang as the Mindanao politician allegedly involved in the smuggling. He said Rimbang was believed to be the financier of the entire operation.
According to Remulla, Rimbang is married to Princess Rohaniah Rimbang, the sister of the wife of alias "Fahad" who was arrested at an airport in Laos.
Rimbang appealed to the government to refrain from disclosing his family’s names and pictures on social media.
He said that his family and children’s lives have been affected.
“Nakikiusap ako sa ating gobyerno na 'wag po natin ilagay sa social media ‘yung mga pangalan namin, ‘yung mga mukha namin na wala namang ebidensya, wala naman tayong ginawang masama,” he said.
(I am appealing to our government not to post our names and faces on social media when there is no evidence and we have done nothing wrong.)
“Pinanganak ako na wala akong naging kaso sa gobyerno, lalo sa droga. Hindi ako nakipagkuntsaba sa mga ilegal na gawain kasi ayaw ko masira ang pangalan ko,” he added.
(I was born without ever having a case against me with the government, especially involving drugs. I never colluded in illegal activities because I don’t want to tarnish my name.)
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has issued subpoenas to 11 persons of interest. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Flu cases rise on west coast earlier than usual as US health experts encourage vaccine
articles.summary:
California flu test rate at 9.65%, higher than normal 1% rate for early October, amid mutation of H1N1 influenza A strain

Flu cases on the west coast are on the rise months earlier than…

blocks.text: Flu cases on the west coast are on the rise months earlier than normal, prompting US health experts to stress the importance of the annual vaccine.
Flu activity typically ramps up in December, hitting its peak in February. But this season has kicked into action earlier this year, with higher positive cases than normal recorded.
Several experts have credited the early seasonal start to a new mutation of the influenza A strain H1N1, which was behind the 2009 swine flu pandemic.
This strain has accounted for 242 of 300 influenza viruses reported by public health laboratories to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to date (CDC).

In California, during the past two flu seasons, influenza test positivity hovered slightly above 1% in early October. As of 10 October, that rate is 9.65%, according to data from the state’s department of health.
As of 11 October, Utah has recorded 242 influenza A cases, up from 10 cases this time last year, according to Germ Watch, an Intermountain Health database.
Parts of central Oregon have also seen an influenza A surge.
Influenza vaccines can reduce severe illness and hospitalization, according to the American Medical Association, which recommends flu shots for all people 6 months and older.
The 2026-27 flu vaccines, approved by the FDA in August, ​target H1N1, H3N2 – the dominant strain last flu season – and one influenza B virus.
Scott Hensley, a microbiologist at the University of Pennsylvania, said two of the three components of this year’s vaccine appear to be very well matched to circulating flu strains.
However, the H1N1 mutation might affect antibodies in younger people, and with flu season picking up steam, “it is probably a good idea to get vaccinated early”, Hensley said via ​email.
Promotion of flu shots has been reduced under US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, a longtime anti-vaccine activist who has engineered an overhaul of long-standing childhood vaccine schedules.
Reuters contributed reporting

articles.title: ‘I’ve killed someone’: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly confessed to friend and asked for help moving bodies, court told
articles.summary:
Friend tells jury Lamarre-Condon told him in early 2024 ‘I shot the first one through the head and the second one through the door’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly confessed to killing two men, telling his friend it was an “out-of-body experience”, before attempting to play it off as a joke, a court has been told.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Lamarre-Condon’s friend, whose identity is suppressed, told the New South Wales supreme court on Friday that the officer arrived at his workplace the day Baird and Davies were killed.
Lamarre-Condon told him, “I’ve done something”, and when the friend asked for an explanation, the policeman said “I’ve killed someone”, the jury was told.
“I said ‘Are you fucking kidding me?’, he said, ‘I wish I was’,” the friend told the court. “He said it just felt like an out-of-body experience and it just wasn’t him.”
The friend said when he asked how Lamarre-Condon did it, the officer said with a gun.
He then made a gesture with his fingers indicating a firearm and said “pew pew”, the friend told the court.
When asked for more details, Lamarre-Condon allegedly said: “I shot the first one through the head and the second one through the door.”
Lamarre-Condon then said the second person wasn’t meant to be shot but he “couldn’t leave any witnesses”, the friend told the jury.
The officer asked his friend to leave work to help clean up and move the bodies, the court heard.
The friend then returned to his workplace and explained the situation to his team lead, who told him to tell Lamarre-Condon he had a meeting he couldn’t miss.
Lamarre-Condon later messaged the friend and asked “I should get an Oscar, hey?” before going on video call and saying “Got you”.
When the friend got upset, Lamarre-Condon said, “it’s not a fucking joke, you’re mentally fucking with me”, the court was told.
The policeman responded: “OK it is real but I just didn’t want you to tell anyone.”
Earlier on Friday, the friend revealed he had travelled overseas in late 2023 for a trip with Lamarre-Condon.
He said that while overseas, Lamarre-Condon told the friend: “I need to find a spot … to purchase a silencer.”
The officer explained he was going hunting on a mate’s farm, the jury was told.
The two found what they believed to be a gun store, but it had either closed down or there had been a fake ad, the friend said.
after newsletter promotion
The friend returned to Australia before Lamarre-Condon and soon after received a photo from the officer showing multiple airsoft guns.
The witness on Friday said he asked if Lamarre-Condon had found what he was looking for and the officer said: “No, it was an airsoft gun shop, no suppressor there.”
Back in Sydney, Lamarre-Condon drove his friend to a national park and took a police service weapon out of a paper bag, the jury was told.
Lamarre-Condon gave his friend a police-issued radio and asked him to listen for any reports of police movement towards them after the officer shot the firearm.

“I said, ‘You can’t really shoot your police-issued firearm.’ He then told me that they were training bullets he had taken previously from a police shoot they do once a year,” the friend told the court.
He said Lamarre-Condon then fired the weapon and asked his friend how loud it was.
He tried again, shooting a bullet into the bushland before asking “does this make any difference on the sound?”, the jury heard.
“He’s asked me whether it would be louder or would you hear this in a house?” the friend said on Friday. “I proceeded to say ‘You could hear that anywhere, it was super loud’.”
On their way home, Lamarre-Condon then allegedly said, “you can’t tell anyone about this”, the court heard.
The defence team claims Baird and Davies were accidentally shot when the accused acted in “self-defence”.
Lamarre-Condon then “panicked considerably”, cleaning up the scene and disposing of the bodies, defence lawyer John Stratton SC said.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: Why affordable smartphones matter to a mobile-first PH economy
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – As demand for AI infrastructure puts pressure on memory-chip supplies, affordable smartphones are becoming a necessity as prices on new devices face mounting cost pressures…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – As demand for AI infrastructure puts pressure on memory-chip supplies, affordable smartphones are becoming a necessity as prices on new devices face mounting cost pressures worldwide.
With more everyday activities moving online, rising smartphone costs could make it harder for some Filipinos to access digital services.
A mobile-first Philippines
A July 2026 report by the Statista Research Department tracked the growth of smartphone users in the Philippines, with the number increasing by 40.43 million between 2010 and 2025.
DataReportal’s 2025 report estimated that 97.5 million people in the Philippines used the internet.
Then, DataReportal’s 2026 report recorded 137 million mobile connections in the Philippines, compared with an estimated population of 117 million.
These data show how Filipinos are constantly online and activate numerous devices for their day-to-days.
RELATED STORY: Only 17% of Philippine businesses have a roadmap to scale AI
Long-term economy effects

A roundtable discussion facilitated by Charles Cole Navarro, Principal Investment Associate of the Asian Development Bank examined the market demand for a mobile-first economy and the threat rising prices can create for Filipino livelihood.

blocks.caption: From left to right: Dr. Jonathan Illagan, Psychologist, Consumer Insights Researcher , and Co-Founder of Groundwork, Jelmer David Ikink, Managing Partner of Foxmont Capital Partners, Randy Lim, Vice President, Device and Cards Management at Globe Telecom, Karl Loo, Founder and CEO of 3Cat,  Charl…

blocks.text: Jelmer David Ikink, Managing Partner of Foxmont Capital Partners, mentions how Filipinos will be affected in the long term.
As applications evolve and require more processing power and storage, older smartphones may struggle to keep up or lose compatibility with newer software.

“If a phone gets more expensive, then it heavily affects their income. So the impact can be quite substantial,” said Ikink. “Old software means an app will stop working because developers can’t keep maintaining apps that handle old softwares. This makes a direct impact.
Apple’s latest line was a 20% price hike compared to previous generations.
The pressure could continue if memory-chip supplies fail to keep pace with demand.

“Memory chip prices have soared. For phones under 400 dollars, the memory cost is 60 percent of the device. For phones that are 100 dollars, they are unprofitable. If memory chips stabilize, they will continue to be unprofitable,” said Ikink.
What it means for Filipinos
As smartphones become increasingly important to everyday life, Filipino consumers must weigh the cost of a device against the features and capabilities they need.
A 2022 study presented at the De La Salle University Senior High School Research Congress examined how consumers weighed a smartphone’s practicality against its price.
In the same year, another study published in ResearchGate wrote how Filipinos extensively research before they purchase devices in Shopee or Lazada.

But since then, the age of AI has also affected consumer priorities. Samsung’s survey in the Philippines in 2026 saw that two out of three Filipinos are now leaning towards phones with AI capabilities.
Dr. Jonathan Illagan, Psychologist, Consumer Insights Researcher , and Co-Founder of Groundwork echoed the sentiments of Filipino priorities over price.

“When it comes to priorities, what do I need to protect? All our needs remain the same, we want to stay in touch with people, we have work, children have school, we have to fill up government papers,” said Illagan.
“Daily life is migrating to this digital space. Having good devices becomes an expense they have to protect. Confidence becomes part of the value.”
Illagan said consumers may be willing to spend more on devices that meet their needs.

“People might be willing to spend more when it addresses their priorities. Access to connectivity is different from meeting full participation,” he explained. “If they are unable to access certain tools, they will be left behind.”
Solution, sustainability, and the secondhand market
Telecommunications companies and other industry players have introduced programs to make smartphone purchases more affordable.
Randy Lim, Vice President, Device and Cards Management at Globe Telecom laid out their plans and programs that can keep connectivity cost low.
Lim said these efforts aim to bridge the device affordability gap. Globe’s Gadget Xchange program allows their postpaid subscribers to trade in or replace their devices.
To replace a device, however, means that old devices need to go somewhere else.
Lim, Illagan, and Ikink echoed that the rising prices of smartphones also equates to a problem in sustainability.
Foxmont Capital Partners partnered and brought 3Cat to open in the Philippines.
3Cat is a Malaysia-based platform that sells refurbished devices. Through 3Cat, devices go through a rigorous diagnostic process and necessary repairs before being sold in the market.
“Second tech becomes the first choice,” said Karl Loo, Founder and CEO of 3Cat.

“What 3Cat tries to do is eliminate the middleman. We buy demo units, switch it out, work with telcos that would provide us trade-in stocks. 3Cat runs trade-in programs with retailers that’s getting it from a reliable source,” said Loo. “We have a diagnostics software that ensures this. We also invest in its repairs before we repackage.”

In 2022, the United Nations reported that the Philippines recorded over 540 million kilograms in e-waste. A 2026 study in Denmark by Aalborg University saw that one out of three usable mobile phones are thrown away.
While the Philippines has its own market for secondhand phones, the idea of refurbished phones can still make consumers wary.
“Secondhand is a viable first choice,” said Loo. 3Cat’s formal approach to selling secondhand devices includes payment plans and guarantees.
“Isn’t a downgrade, but it can give you access to premium devices,” echoed Illagan.
As smartphones continue to surge, practical and sustainable solutions become the best choice to continuously build the Philippines’ digital economy.

articles.title: Embattled QLD Mininster Amanda Camm quits Crisafulli frontbench citing health and safety reasons
articles.summary:
Camm, who resigned following months of pressure over her handling of state’s child safety system, cited Helen Haines attack as reason for departure

Queensland minister Amanda Camm has…

blocks.text: Queensland minister Amanda Camm has resigned from cabinet following months of pressure over the state government’s handling of the child safety system and efforts to prevent domestic and family violence.
Camm told reporters on Friday the decision to step down was “mine alone”.
She suggested that some criticism of her had gone beyond “public scrutiny and accountability” and cited the recent alleged attack on federal MP Helen Haines.
Over the past year she had experienced harassment, threats, bullying and vilification, she said.

Camm had recently taken six weeks of medical leave, including undergoing a surgical procedure. She said she had realised her recovery would be “ongoing” and that she would not be able to continue perform her ministerial duties, given the workload and “the ongoing stresses”.
“It would be unfair to the government for me to take further leave,” Camm said.
A replacement is expected to be announced later on Friday.

Before taking leave, Camm had been the government’s most under-pressure minister. Her relationship with Tim Mander, the sport and Olympics minister, had placed both under scrutiny in parliament and the press.
But it was her dual responsibilities – child safety and the prevention of family violence – that had heaped pressure on Camm over her job performance.

The government came under fire over claims of children in state care sleeping on the floor of government offices, which child protection workers linked to government policies including the cancelling of contracts to some residential care providers.
Camm also came under pressure over budget cuts to domestic and family violence prevention, and a lack of progress on reforms demanded by the former government’s women’s safety and justice taskforce.
after newsletter promotion

Guardian Australia reported that Camm had buried the findings of a panel of domestic and family violence victim-survivors, which was highly critical of police. Her office told one member she was no longer welcome to contact them by phone.
Camm said the attack on Haines had “reinforced the importance of taking concerns about personal health, safety and wellbeing of people in public life very seriously”.

“Public scrutiny and accountability are central to democracy and to our institutions. Harassment, threats, bullying and personal vilification are not. And for the past year this has been my experience. There is much more work to be done.”
The premier, David Crisafulli, said he wanted to “support Amanda” and that she had not been removed over her performance.
It is understood that the government will not instigate a broader reshuffle but will appoint a new face to the ministry to replace Camm.
Among those considered in the frame for a promotion is former senator and Morrison government figure Amanda Stoker, who was elected to the state parliament in 2024.

articles.title: The haunting call of Canada's common loon is becoming less common amid widespread declines, study suggests
articles.summary: A new study published Thursday in the journal FACETS reveals severe declines in loon chick populations across North America over the past three decades or more.

image.caption: A common loon baby rests on its parent's back on a lake in northwestern Ontario in July 2026. A new study published Thursday in the journal FACETS reveals severe declines in loon chick populations across North America over the past three decades or more. (Bryce Hoye/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba
A new study published Thursday in the journal FACETS reveals severe declines in loon chick populations across North America over the past three decades or more.
Prairies, Atlantic provinces among North American regions seeing steepest drops
It's a haunting sound synonymous with nightfall in the summer when an eerie calm spreads over glassy wetlands and cottage country lake surfaces across Canada.

But the trembling call of the common loon may be getting less common amid "substantial" North American declines, new research suggests — with Prairie and Atlantic populations suffering among the steepest losses.
"The most alarming thing is the extent of this decline," said Matthew Fuirst, an ecologist with Birds Canada and one of the authors of a study published Thursday in the journal FACETS.

Canada is home to 94 per cent of the global common loon population, with an estimated 254,000 breeding couples (half a million individuals) that migrate north to make the next generation every spring.

The iconic species, a minted representation of which many Canadians routinely carry around in their pockets and purses, has faced threats before — from DDT to lead-based fishing tackle and mercury poisoning.
From the CBC archives: Lost loons (1971)
Now, the latest team of nearly two dozen collaborators from Canada and the U.S. cite climate change among a list of possible drivers for declines in loon chicks.

The study analyzes loon breeding data from 3,421 lakes the past three or so decades, half of which came from thousands of volunteer observations as part of the long-running citizen science effort, the Canadian Lakes Loon Survey.
There were "significant declines" in how many chicks were observed in that time in a majority of regions.
Loon chick productivity rate was a benchmark measure defined by researchers as observations of six-week-old young across nearly 46,000 observations of loon pairs.
The study suggests a 40 per cent average drop in loon chick productivity in 10 of 12 study areas — including in B.C. and Ontario — over the past three or so decades.

Loon chick productivity sank even more starkly by 65 per cent across Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba since the early 1990s. Meanwhile, Canada's East Coast saw a 74 per cent reduction, according to researchers.
Quebec and the state of Maine were the only regions where chick productivity seemed more or less stable.
A common loon range map that appeared in the new FACETS journal article documenting loon declines in North America. (FACETS journal)

The team notes that while the loon chick population isn't the only measure of how healthy or stable the population is, the long-term declines could "signal looming population declines" in the Prairies, Ontario, Atlantic Canada and in New York, Massachusetts and New Hampshire.
The researchers looked at nearly 46,000 instances of loon pairs observed on a given lake and where eggs or chicks were recorded, but no six-week-old chicks were seen.

"This study design is very strong, and frankly, I consider the results that they are presenting here as being alarming," said Nicola Koper, dean of the faculty of environment at University of Northern British Columbia, who was not part of the study.
Koper is co-author of Best Places to Bird in the Prairies and she was professor of conservation biology for nearly two decades at the University of Manitoba before moving on to UNBC.
She said the losses are dramatic on their own, but the fact they've happened over only three decades is startling.

"Some [readers] will be 30 years old, and so if they think back to whether they feel like they saw more loons with babies when they were younger, the chances are that that's accurate, that they have themselves observed this change," said Koper.
Climate change behind declines
The research team says the cause of the declines may vary depending on the region and that unknown is something they're digging into now, said Fuirst.
But in all cases the losses are propelled by human activity.

items: Fewer loons on your lake? It may be due to climate change

blocks.text: "Human development and the development of shorelines, the environmental contaminants from climate change is another threat we're experiencing, " said Fuirst.
"As climate change influences weather patterns, the rain which is acidic makes the lake more acidic and thus reducing the amount of fish that are available for those loons."
A common loon baby rests on its parent's back in northwestern Ontario in July 2026. (Bryce Hoye/CBC)
Warmer temperatures associated with climate change have also brought more rain and storm events to loon habitat.
That could be destroying low-lying loon nests or drowning eggs during flood events when waters rise or are disturbed from violent wave action, said Koper.
Recent research from the U.S. Midwest has also made a connection between poor loon health and lower water clarity, which can arise from sediment running into lakes as a result of more frequent rains.
That makes it harder for loons to see and hunt their minnow, crayfish and other prey in the water, said Fuirst.
"It's this domino effect of climate change basically down to water quality," he said.

The study pooled together Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba data into a single Prairie category because there wasn't enough data to analyze loon numbers confidently in each of those regions on their own.

items: For the birds: Manitobans pick loon to grace specialty licence plate

blocks.text: Koper said that may be more a reflection of how many of the many lakes in the Prairies are inaccessible to volunteers or otherwise unpopulated.
Fuirst said anglers should opt for lead-free, less-toxic tackle options, boaters should avoid disturbing loons and cottagers should ensure shorelines remain as natural as possible.
"The everyday person can take several actions to help steward lakes and the loons that they rely on," he said.

Koper encourages people concerned by the findings to take action and get involved in citizen science projects like the Canadian Lakes Loon Survey and "advocate with ... politicians about the importance of climate change and how it's impacting our wildlife and our lives."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Bryce Hoye is a multi-platform journalist with a background in wildlife biology. He has worked for CBC Manitoba for over a decade with stints producing at CBC's Quirks & Quarks and Front Burner. He was a 2024-25 Knight Science Journalism Fellow at MIT. He is also Prairie rep for outCBC. He has won a national Radio Television Digital News Association award for a 2017 feature on the history of the fur trade, and a 2023 Prairie region award for an audio documentary about a Chinese-Canadian father passing down his love for hockey to the next generation of Asian Canadians.

articles.title: Department of Justice opens criminal investigation into Corey Lewandowski
articles.summary:
Ex-Trump adviser and former top aide for homeland security alleged to have profited off government role

Corey Lewandowski, a former political adviser to Donald Trump and ⁠top aide at the…

blocks.text: Corey Lewandowski, a former political adviser to Donald Trump and ⁠top aide at the Department ⁠of Homeland Security, ​is under criminal investigation over allegations he profited off his role in the US government, three US officials and a fourth person familiar with the matter told Reuters ⁠on Thursday.

The investigation began with a criminal referral to the justice department from the internal watchdog at DHS, according to the four people. The DHS inspector general’s office has been investigating ⁠Lewandowski’s involvement in the handling of certain government contracts, according to one of the people, a DHS official.

A lawyer ​for Lewandowski, Adam Trigg, did not immediately respond to ‌a request for comment. The ‌investigation was first reported in the Wall Street Journal, which quoted Lewandowski’s lawyer as saying that his client denies ‌all allegations of wrongdoing.
The DoJ has not yet issued subpoenas or other legal demands in the criminal investigation, according to one of the people. All four of the people spoke on the condition of anonymity.

The justice department under Trump has investigated several prominent critics of the president, including the former FBI director James Comey and the New York attorney general Letitia James, but investigations of people close to Trump have been rare. The department has also moved ‌to dismiss several existing cases involving Trump allies, including supporters charged in connection with the 6 January 2021 attack on the US Capitol.
Asked about media reports on the investigation, Trump told reporters ​that he did not know the specifics of the investigation, but said: “I want my people to be honest.”
“And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DoJ go and do whatever they have to do,” Trump added.

Lewandowski served as a top aide to the former homeland security secretary Kristi Noem during her tenure leading DHS. Trump fired Noem in March after ⁠months of controversy, including the fatal shootings of two US citizens by federal officers ​in Minneapolis and lawmakers’ questions over a $220m advertising contract promoting Noem that was ​awarded without a standard bidding process.

Lewandowski had signed some DHS contracts despite having questionable legal authority ​as a special government ‌employee, according to the ​DHS official. Certain grants ​and contracts, including those involving the Federal Emergency Management Agency, were put on hold at Lewandowski’s direction, according to two of the people, both of whom are DHS officials.
Lewandowski previously served as a campaign manager during Trump’s first presidential run in 2016 and advised his 2024 campaign.

articles.title: Execution staff warned of possibility some of Christa Pike's veins had 'blown': attorney
articles.summary: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike's arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or…

image.caption: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike is seen in a 2023 booking photograph. Pike survived an attempted execution on Sept. 30, including two doses of pentobarbital that were administered to her. Pike's attorney has said in a court document that execution team members failed multiple times to establish workin

blocks.text: World·New

Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike's arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or "blown," before she was injected with the lethal drug, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday.
Defence says IV team went through about 10 needles, tried several IV sites

The IV team went through about 10 needles and tried several IV sites on both arms, attorney Randy Spivey wrote in the document, which provides the most detailed account of the execution attempt so far. They even struggled to push saline through the last IV site they established, Spivey wrote.

Pike, 50, was hospitalized after surviving two doses of pentobarbital as the state tried to execute her on Sept. 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. She was 18 when she tortured and killed Slemmer with her boyfriend, becoming one of the youngest women to be sentenced to death.
No protocol for those who survive 2nd injection
State protocol calls for a second dose of pentobarbital if the first doesn't result in death, but it doesn't spell out what to do if a person survives the second injection.

After being taken to a hospital, Pike was on a ventilator for several days. At one point, her attorneys did not expect her to survive. She ultimately regained consciousness and returned to prison after being discharged.

items: Emergency medical help for Christa Pike was delayed due to confusion, 911 tapes reveal
Christa Pike discharged from hospital after surviving execution attempt, attorney says

blocks.text: The failed execution has brought renewed scrutiny to how Tennessee carries out death sentences. The court document was part of a separate legal proceeding in which people on the state's death row are challenging Tennessee's lethal injection procedures.

"Our predictions about the likelihood of botched executions have come true — and will continue to come true — without substantial change," said Kit Thomas, an attorney representing people on death row in the case.
'Wincing and grimacing'

The execution team began trying to place the two IVs required by Tennessee's execution protocols at 6:34 p.m., Spivey wrote, and when they struggled Pike helped, advising them to look in her upper arm for a viable vein.
They managed to set an IV in Pike's right arm within about six minutes, but it took them nearly an hour to complete the same process in her left arm.
Pike was "wincing and grimacing" as the IV team members moved the needles around inside her left arm, Spivey wrote, and the team members repeatedly expressed doubts after inserting the needles.

One team member said a vein "might be blowing" at 6:57 p.m. while examining an IV in Pike's left arm, but two others said they couldn't tell, Spivey wrote. "One of them said something like, ‘it's either blood or blown, I need to know,'" Spivey wrote.
The team tried again with a different spot in her left arm, and the needle appeared to be severely bent when they pulled it out, the attorney said.
"I think it's blown," the attorney recalled one of the IV team members saying at 7:07 p.m.
After more attempts, the team decided at 7:13 p.m. that they had successfully placed an IV in Pike's left arm, and they taped her hands down and hooked her up to a heart monitor.
Complained of pain
A series of phone calls were made to the execution chamber starting about five minutes later.

Spivey said it appeared the execution team members responsible for pushing the pentobarbital into the lines — a process that happens in an adjoining room — were asking the IV team for repeated checks of Pike's left arm.
Emergency vehicles are seen arriving at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, Tenn., on Sept. 30, after the execution of Christa Pike was halted. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)
It's not clear exactly when the pentobarbital was pushed into the IV lines, but at 7:34 p.m., Pike said her arm was hurting.

"I feel like my arm is about to bust. It burns," she said, according to her attorney. She continued to talk to her spiritual adviser for the next 10 minutes before she began making an "agitated snoring sound," Spivey wrote.

Over the next 30 minutes Pike strained, flinched, moved her head and seemed to struggle to breathe, Spivey said, and when he asked to use a phone he was led on a circuitous, seven-minute route through the facility instead of being allowed to use the phone in the execution witness room.

Spivey called fellow attorneys at 8:22 p.m. and asked them to stop the execution because a third dose of pentobarbital isn't authorized under the state's protocol. He then went back to the witness room and told the deputy attorney general that Pike needed immediate medical care.

Spivey was told an ambulance was on the way at 8:50 p.m., and 20 minutes later he was told that medical staff were providing life-saving measures, he wrote. An ambulance was seen arriving at the hospital at 9:14 p.m.

articles.title: Signal No. 2 still up over Batanes, parts of Babuyan Islands as 'Rosal' keeps strength
articles.summary: Signal No. 2 remains in Batanes and parts of the Babuyan Islands as Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) maintains strength over the sea northeast of Batanes, PAGASA said Friday.

blocks.text: October 23, 2026 | 8:34am
Satellite rendering shows Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) taken as of 4:30 a.m. of Oct. 23, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains in effect over Batanes and the northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands as Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) maintained its strength while moving northwestward over the sea east-northeast of Batanes, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Friday.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Friday, October 23, PAGASA said Rosal was packing maximum sustained winds of 155 kilometers per hour near the center and gusts of up to 190 kph.
The typhoon was last spotted 275 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, moving northwestward at 15 kph.
Strong to typhoon-force winds extend up to 900 kilometers from the center.
Warning signals
PAGASA raised the following tropical cyclone wind signals:
Signal No. 2
Luzon

items: Batanes
Northeastern portion of Babuyan Islands (Babuyan, Panuitan, Calayan and Camiguin islands)

blocks.text: Residents in these areas may experience gale-force winds ranging from 62 to 88 kph within the next 24 hours, posing minor to moderate threats to life and property.
Signal No. 1

items: Rest of the Babuyan Islands
Mainland Cagayan
Northeastern portion of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, San Pablo and Palanan)
Ilocos Norte
Apayao

blocks.text: Residents in these areas may experience strong winds ranging from 39 to 61 kph within the next 36 hours, posing minimal to minor threats to life and property.
The northeast monsoon and Rosal's outer circulation will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas:

items: Friday, October 23: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Camiguin, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.
Saturday, October 24: Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Polillo Islands, Bicol Region, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo and Negros Occidental.
Sunday, October 25: Batanes and Babuyan Islands.

blocks.text: Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the seaboards of Northern Luzon and the eastern seaboards of Central and Southern Luzon.
Very rough to very high seas, with waves reaching up to 12 meters, are expected along the northern and eastern seaboards of Batanes.

Waves may reach up to 9 meters along the remaining seaboards of Batanes and up to 8 meters along the northern and eastern seaboards of the Babuyan Islands and the northeastern seaboard of mainland Cagayan.

Seas may reach up to 6 meters along the remaining seaboards of the Babuyan Islands and mainland Cagayan, the seaboard of northern Isabela and the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte. Waves may reach up to 5.5 meters along the remaining seaboard of Isabela and up to 5 meters along the remaining seaboard of Ilocos Norte.

Waves may reach up to 4.5 meters along the seaboards of northern Ilocos Sur and northern Aurora, the northern seaboards of Camarines Sur and Camarines Norte, and the northern and eastern seaboards of the Polillo Islands and Catanduanes.

PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types of vessels in areas where very rough to very high seas are expected. Mariners were advised to remain in port or seek shelter in a safe harbor until winds and waves subside.
Operators of small vessels, including motorbancas, were also advised against venturing out to sea under rough conditions, especially if their vessels are ill-equipped or they lack experience.
Track, intensity
Rosal is expected to continue moving generally northwestward until Saturday, October 24, before moving northward and then north-northeastward between Saturday and Sunday, October 25.
On its forecast track, the typhoon is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by early Saturday.

PAGASA said Rosal is forecast to weaken gradually within the next 24 hours before weakening rapidly. It may be downgraded into a severe tropical storm by Saturday morning and further weaken into a tropical storm by Saturday evening.

articles.title: What is PHP, and how did a flaw in its code lead several websites to go dark this week?
articles.summary: PHP is an open-source computer language that powers an estimated 70 per cent of the internet. While websites being taken offline caused alarm, that was done to implement a fix — which cybersecurity…

image.caption: PHP is an open-source computer language that's widely used across the internet. (Dado Ruvic/Reuters)

blocks.text: A vulnerability in a critical piece of the internet's infrastructure was exposed this week, sending website operators worldwide scrambling to implement a fix.

The problem resided in part of the PHP coding language — a commonly used software that's "the backbone of the internet," according to Isaac Privett, a senior penetration tester at Toronto-based cybersecurity firm Packetlabs.
And the vulnerability had been there for years, potentially allowing bad actors to access sites, make changes to them and harvest data.

items: Canadian government sites among those offline after flaw identified in widely used computer language

blocks.text: The issue prompted many to take their websites offline while they implemented a fix, causing some websites — including government ones in Canada — to go dark.
Here's what you need to know about the PHP language, how it came to light and how serious the vulnerability is.
What is PHP?

PHP is an open-source computer language — meaning anyone can download and use it for free — that's widely used across the internet. The tech is managed by the non-profit PHP Foundation, with a team of volunteer board members and a handful of developers.

When you visit a website, a lot of pieces of information, such as images, links and what colour a site should appear in, all need to be assembled and displayed correctly to end users, explains technology analyst Carmi Levy. That's the job PHP does, Levy says, pulling those elements together and bringing websites to life.

"PHP is silently working in the background to make sure that websites make it from disjointed data sitting on a server somewhere to a live website that you can interact with on the browser, on the device that is sitting in front of you," said Levy, who's based in London, Ont.

Wiz, one of the cybersecurity firms that helped identify the issue, estimates that about 70 per cent of websites are powered by PHP, while web technology tracker W3Techs puts the figure at 75 per cent.
A programmer works with PHP code at RK Solutions software development company in Guernica, Spain, on Thursday. (Vincent West/Reuters)

That widespread use makes the tech a "foundational" piece of technology for the internet to function, Levy said, and that's why a vulnerability with it can have potentially wide-reaching consequences.
What's the problem, and how was it discovered?

A group of researchers from two cybersecurity companies — Calif and Wiz — released blog posts Wednesday, saying they had found two vulnerabilities in PHP. The researchers had been working as part of an OpenAI program to detect potential vulnerabilities across the internet, including within PHP.

Ryan Austin, a cybersecurity researcher at Calif.io who helped identify the problems, says he was aware of a 2004 security issue with PHP and sent OpenAI's GPT‑5.6 Sol to look in the same part of PHP's code for other potential bugs.
"And then a few days later, we managed to find something pretty serious," Austin said.
The PHP Foundation explained in a Wednesday release that both issues sit in "parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling."
Austin explains that when PHP encounters an error, it leaves behind memory details that can be corrupted and potentially give hackers a way into sites.
Tech analyst Carmi Levy says the fact that PHP is used so widely across the internet is part of what makes a vulnerability with it so concerning. (Submitted by Carmi Levy)

Once inside, hackers would be able to make changes to the websites — potentially installing malware or removing content from the sites — or to read sensitive data such as passwords, according to Levy.

Wiz said the vulnerabilities had existed for more than a decade. PHP Foundation acknowledged that a researcher had theorized this possible exploit in 2024, but no concrete way to enact it was found at the time.
PHP Foundation said the delay in implementing a solution was a "structural failure" caused by a lack of resources and the security team's decision process.
How serious is it?
Levy likens it to if one of the most popular makers of locks for doors discovered a master key was widely available to use.
"So someone could literally walk up to your front door, put that master key in, and they could gain access to your home," Levy said.

He explains security incidents are scored on a scale from zero to 10 using something called the Common Vulnerability Scoring System. These ones ranked as a 9.2, which Levy says means they're quite serious.
Websites around world taken down after flawed code opens them up to hackers
"One vulnerability in a technology that almost everybody uses means there's a potential global impact here," Levy said.
From Austin's perspective, it's "probably one of the worst vulnerabilities that I've ever seen."
How is it being fixed?
Cybersecurity experts say the good news is that a solution exists.
PHP Foundation released patches for the vulnerability on Wednesday and urged those who use it in their websites to implement the fix as soon as possible.
Government cybersecurity agencies and government leaders around the world, including in Canada, echoed that call.

Many websites, including government ones from Canada, France and Japan, went dark while the potential security issue was remedied. Provincial sites for Newfoundland and Labrador and Prince Edward Island were down for the day, for example, but both appeared to be running again on Thursday.
The U.S. National Security Agency's cyber unit called for any organizations that couldn't patch the issue immediately to take their websites offline until the fix could be put in place.

While websites going down caused some panic, Levy says the story has a silver lining. Those sites were taken down temporarily out of an abundance of caution after researchers identified a vulnerability before hackers did, and Levy says that shows the system for flagging these kinds of things is working.
The Newfoundland and Labrador government site was offline on Wednesday after the PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed. (CBC)

Some sites experienced hack attempts after the vulnerability was made public, but those didn't appear to work. Cloudflare's CEO, for example, said on social media that the Cloudflare network experienced tens of thousands of attempts to exploit the flaw within 45 minutes of the announcement being made and "hundreds of thousands" within two hours.
On Wednesday, PHP Foundation told CBC News in an email they hadn't seen any evidence of hackers being able to successfully exploit the vulnerability.
Do I need to take action?

Cybersecurity experts say because the issue affects the back end of websites, the onus is mostly on those who run them — like businesses or other organizations — to make sure they're implementing the fix.
That's fairly straightforward for website operators to do in most cases — somewhat like updating a personal computer, according to Privett from Packetlabs.
"You just have to upgrade to the newest version of PHP, and that seems to handle 99 per cent of your problems," Privett said.
AI can make cyberattacks faster and smarter

But because the vulnerability and the fix have been made public for quite some time now, Privett says website owners will need to be on watch for indicators of possible breaches that could have happened before they were able to put the patches in place.
"It's always a good idea that after you patch, just to look for indicators of compromise in case that someone got in your system using that bug," Privett said.
Privett also encourages consumers who have their own websites or apps to double check whether they use PHP to make sure that they're protected.

And for all consumers, Levy says they can protect themselves from any potential kind of data breach by maximizing their own personal digital safety protocols. Practicing good password hygiene — by changing passwords often and not reusing them — and activating two-factor authentication, for example, help ensure that even if hackers were to access your data on a breached website, they wouldn't be as effective at using that information against you.

articles.title: ICC prosecutors seek admission of 3 more recorded testimonies vs Rodrigo Duterte
articles.summary: The prosecution panel in the crimes against humanity charges against former President Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court to admit the recorded testimonies of three more…

blocks.text: Published October 23, 2026 8:25am

The prosecution panel in the crimes against humanity charges against former President Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court to admit the recorded testimonies of three more witnesses.
In a 12-page application, the Office of the Prosecutor said granting the request will expedite the proceedings by reducing the length of the witnesses' direct examination.
It added that the prior recorded testimonies of witnesses P-0008, P-1164, and P-1303 are relevant, reliable, and probative.

"The Three Witnesses’ evidence further goes to the proof of the contextual elements of crimes against humanity and to the policy to ‘neutralise’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines," it said.

It further said that "the introduction into evidence of the Prior Recorded Testimonies is not prejudicial to or inconsistent with the rights of the Accused, as the witnesses will be available for cross-examination by the Defence and any further questioning by the Chamber, the parties, and the Common Legal Representatives of Victims."
The prosecution said it obtained the recorded testimonies of the three witnesses during the investigation, when they were interviewed.
It added that the three were informed of the voluntary nature of their interviews and of their rights.
"At the conclusion of the interviews, the witnesses confirmed that they answered the questions of their own free will and had no complaints about the way the interview was conducted," it said.
The document was signed by acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.
Duterte is detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands. His trial is scheduled for November 30.
The drug war saw at least 6,000 people dead, with rights groups believing that the number could be as high as 30,000. —AOL, GMA News
